description:
We are an ambitious team tackling Idea #9 (Identifying Earth Analogs for Moon Bases & Mars).

Who we are: Students skilled in GIS, spatial analysis, and research.Why join us: Work on high-impact space agency challenges and build cutting-edge comparative studies.Looking for: GIS/Remote Sensing specialists, geologists, developers, and technical writers. Join us to explore space from Earth!
summary:
Twin Worlds is a working web prototype that finds places on Earth that match places on Mars and the Moon, so mission teams can test landers, rovers and base operations before flight. A user picks any spot on Mars or the Moon, chooses the purpose of the test (landing, rover driving, building a base, finding resources or studying ancient lakes), and the app searches 30,311 bare-land areas across the whole Earth in under a second.

Instead of judging by looks, Twin Worlds compares real properties from NASA and ESA data (slope, roughness, relief, basin shape, lighting, aridity, surface brightness and minerals) with the same code on both worlds. It shows the best Earth place for each property, explains what is similar and what is different, and lists what Earth cannot reproduce, such as gravity, vacuum and lunar temperatures.

This matters because known analog sites are few and well studied. Twin Worlds found five candidate basins in Egypt's Western Desert in Earth's top 1% for Jezero Crater, and, without being told, ranked Antarctica's Dry Valleys #85 of 30,311 for a Moon base.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Twin Worlds finds places on Earth to test Moon and Mars missions. A user picks any spot on Mars or the Moon, chooses the test (landing, rover driving, base building, resources or ancient lakes), and the app searches 30,311 bare-land areas on Earth in under a second. It shows the best Earth place for each property, the top 3 for the chosen test, known analog sites for comparison, and what Earth cannot reproduce (gravity, vacuum, lunar temperatures). Users can then compare both places side by side with linked 3D globes, terrain maps and 3D terrain blocks.

HOW IT WORKS

We describe every area with the same terrain signature (slope, roughness, relief, basin shape) using NASA and ESA data, and compute the Mars or Moon target with the same code. Each property is scored separately; slope and roughness compare full distributions, not averages.

RESULTS

Five basins in Egypt's Western Desert rank in Earth's top 1% for Jezero Crater (hypotheses for fieldwork). For a Moon base, the search ranks Antarctica's Dry Valleys, a known analog, #85 of 30,311 on its own. Our ML second opinion, tested only on unseen sites, separates real analogs from ordinary deserts 72% of the time.

IMPACT AND CREATIVITY

It helps agencies find new, cheaper test sites beyond the few well-known ones. It starts from Mars or the Moon and discovers Earth places, answers "analog for what?", and is honest about Earth's limits.

TOOLS

JavaScript, Python, React, Vite, ArcGIS Maps SDK, Three.js, Chart.js; NASA Earthdata, LP DAAC, ASF, PDS.

LIMITS AND FUTURE

Candidates need field validation; minerals cover only part of Earth. Next: expert-calibrated weights, Earth permafrost and caves, and field visits.
